summary: Proof-worth registry entries owned by the sovereign operation control plane.

entries.contract: Eight closed operation schemas and the daemon request, response, and content-free event envelopes expose exact generation-bound operation, resource, tap, artifact, recovery, and same-UID barrier shapes without caller-supplied authority or human-intent fields.
entries.worth: This catches wire drift, missing generation or bound fields, policy leakage, raw-content event leakage, and widening of the four invocation-scoped private external-spawn intent, child-admit, abandon, and finalize actions before any runtime client can depend on them.
entries.guard: Draft 2020-12 schema and fixture validation only; no daemon, native UI, microphone, TCC, or shared runtime

entries.contract: Immediate socket-peer audit identity, generation-stable non-AOS ancestry, exact generation-bound AOS spawn skips, content-free executable evidence, exact reviewed entry-script and two-helper dependency-set byte binding reduced to one canonical digest, and the invocation-scoped listen-microphone grammar derive authority mechanically without trusting caller lineage. The parent-only token admits a child only after dynamic Node.js Foundation SecCode and mapped-vnode verification; only then does the dispatcher write the reviewed in-memory module bundle, and tokenless finalization resolves the exact admitted socket-peer generation. Parent abandon, bounded expiry, and boot recovery terminalize unfinalized prepared operation/resource claims.
entries.worth: This prevents PID reuse, basename/path trust, caller-selected or substituted Node interpreters, raw executable/script/helper identity persistence, substituted reviewed dependencies, token delivery to the child, finalize-before-image-admission, stale prepared microphone claims, and a transient external adapter from escaping its mechanically authenticated owner root.
entries.guard: fake process observations, temporary sockets/files, and disposable Swift typechecks only; no daemon, process signaling, microphone, or TCC use

entries.worth: This catches partial singleton admission, stale subscriber updates, owner widening, mutable host snapshots, false terminal cleanup, replay/CAS drift, and prior-generation residual loss without acquiring a privileged resource.

entries.worth: This catches double operations, microphone authority before persistence/finalization, speech barge-in, early claim release, and cleanup-hidden terminal outcomes without touching a live audio device or TCC.
